commands.name: Check committed output (CI parity)
commands.command: FNSTOOLS_NO_RELEASE_FETCH=1 npm run build && { drift=$(git status --porcelain -- docs index.html); if [ -n "$drift" ]; then echo "STALE -- commit this rebuild:"; echo "$drift"; exit 1; fi; echo "generated output is current"; }
commands.comment: What .github/workflows/website.yml enforces, run locally before pushing. website/docs/ and index.html are committed because Vercel serves them with no build step, so editing packaging/docs/*.md and forgetting to rebuild would ship docs the site never shows. FNSTOOLS_NO_RELEASE_FETCH=1 keeps it reproducible -- otherwise a release published since the last build restamps index.html and reports drift nobody caused. Leaves the rebuild in the working tree; if it fails, that rebuild is what you commit.

commands.name: Syntax-check the tooling
commands.command: node --check tools/build-site.mjs && node --check tools/cms.mjs && echo "tooling parses"
commands.comment: Parse-only check of the two .mjs entrypoints, the first step CI runs. Catches a typo in the generator without waiting for a full build.

commands.name: Docs still needing prose
commands.command: grep -rl 'TODO: no wiki content' ../packaging/docs || echo "every package has hand-written prose"
commands.comment: Lists packages still documented only by their catalog line -- the stubs docs_seed_from_wiki.py wrote for packages the wiki never covered. CI reports the same list in its job summary. Reads packaging/docs/, which is the source of truth for prose.
